comments.author: @teddychalgren
comments.text: Around 1985, an uncle told me something that has stuck with me since 1985. "Nephew, when it comes time for you to retire, it may take a million or more dollars for you to live on, just to make it to the end."  I took that message to heart. Many of the people in these videos thought that working a full-time job, paying their mortgage or rent, utility bills, car notes, insurance and filling tax returns every year would somehow translate into getting to retire at 65, BUT not having saved anything or very little in some sort of retirement account? I heard a lot of regret in their voices (vacations, the Holidays, going out to eat, get it now-pay for it later, etc...) Nearly all companies offer some sort of 401K matching plan, the employee MUST ask about that and take action.  Pensions are becoming a thing of the past, so now it is on the individual to prepare for retirement.  Other relatives told me to NEVER rely on Social Security.
